title: Cabell County: Housing Choice Vouchers in 2025 included 2,729 people in reported households
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Cabell County: Housing Choice Vouchers in 2025 included 2,729 people in reported households
HUD counted 1,300 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Cabell County in 2025.
In Cabell County, 2,729 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 1 from 2,730 in 2024. Those people lived in 1,300 households.
HUD reported 1,396 Housing Choice Vouchers available in the county, and 93% of them were in use, down 1 percentage point from 94% in 2024.
HUD classified the heads of 16% of those households as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $406 a month toward rent and utilities, up $54 from $352 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $14,180, up $926 from $13,254 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families receiving Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. That average covers families who obtained assistance, not applicants still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
